solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Iron anklet finally brought in for one's security

indicators.note: the iron and the anklet's final letter are brought into the word meaning 'for one'

parts.note: 'for one' introduces an example, as 'say' does
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word anklet

explanation.surface: A prisoner's iron ankle shackle is fitted for their own security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is': the 's is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety and security are synonyms: freedom from danger or harm.

clue.text: Rescue curtailed: a European country losing man in barbarous attack?

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the word for rescue loses its last letter

parts.note: to save is to rescue

indicators.note: losing says the word for man comes out of the country's name

parts.note: Germany is a European country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A failed rescue leaves a country without its men, after a brutal assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' shortens SAVE to SAV; 'losing' takes MAN out of GERMANY, leaving GERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Savagery is brutal, uncivilised violence; a barbarous attack is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sports body going to college in London? Not so

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football
the LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A rumour that a sports federation is moving to a London college, denied.
explanation.walkthrough: The London School of Economics (LSE) is a famous college of London University.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is not so; false is a direct synonym for that phrase.

clue.text: Metal part of fork trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, so the last letter goes from the word for a fork's prong

parts.note: a tine is a prong, part of a fork

explanation.surface: A piece of a metal fork has been cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is a soft silvery metallic element, so an example of a metal.

clue.text: Monitor arranged play-pens

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of play-pens are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on toddlers' play-pens that have been set out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monitor' looks like a verb about watching children; it is a noun, an aircraft that watches.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconnaissance aircraft is a device for monitoring an enemy from the air.

clue.text: Maybe iodine isn't found in variety of sapphire

indicators.note: the iodine's letter is missing from the gem's letters
variety of says the remaining letters of sapphire are rearranged

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A gemmologist muses that a type of blue gem may lack iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of SAPPHIRE and rearrange the other seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are synonyms: both express possibility rather than certainty.

clue.text: Trashed male Puritan, one offering vision of heaven

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters of male Puritan are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunken Puritan man claims to see heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trashed' can mean drunk, which fits the surface, but it is the rearrangement signal; 'heaven' here means the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed theatre projecting images of the stars offers a view of the heavens, the night sky.

clue.text: Politician upset writer embraced by a BBC chief, improvising

indicators.note: the politician and upturned writer sit inside the BBC chief's letters

parts.note: the BBC's head is its Director-General, DG
Lib is short for Liberal, a politician

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word for writer runs backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A politician knocks over a writer while being hugged by a BBC boss, making it up as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NIB to BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-libbing is speaking or performing without preparation, which is improvising.

clue.text: Current navigational device not accommodating first polar direction

indicators.note: not accommodating means not having room for, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a sextant measures angles for navigation
S, south, is a polar direction, here the device's first letter

explanation.surface: A modern navigation instrument that won't show the nearest pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a sea current for a navigator; it means present-day.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still existing, so present and current rather than lost.

clue.text: Live to support son — disregarding daughter?

indicators.note: in a down clue the second word sits below and so supports the first

parts.note: to live is to exist

explanation.surface: A parent lives to support their son and ignores their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring a son and ignoring a daughter because of gender is an example of prejudice by sex.

clue.text: Suggest true love doesn't run smooth around November

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed around the abbreviation for November
echoing 'the course of true love never did run smooth', the letters of true love are jumbled

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean lament that romance always hits trouble, here in late autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't run smooth' rearranges TRUELOVE to VOLUTEER, and 'around' puts that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer an idea or opinion is to offer or put it forward unprompted, as a suggestion.

clue.text: Assign full set of religious texts?

parts.note: a full set is all of them
OT is the Old Testament, a body of religious texts

explanation.surface: A request to hand out a complete set of scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot something is to give out or distribute it as a share: synonym of assign.

clue.text: Hazard visitors will move tail-ender forward before one end to game

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for visitors is shifted further forward in that word

parts.note: visitors to your home are guests
I is the Roman numeral one
checkmate, or mate, ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: A cricket-flavoured scene: visitors push their tail-ender up the order to finish the match.
explanation.walkthrough: A tail-ender is a weak batsman batting last in cricket; here it is just the last letter, S, moved to make GUESST.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard is to venture a rough guess, which is what an estimate made by guesswork amounts to.

clue.text: Part of team kit not entirely given makeover in swindle

indicators.note: not entirely means not quite whole, so the last letter goes

parts.note: shorts are part of a football team's kit
a makeover is a change

explanation.surface: A sports team's strip, partly redesigned, turns out to be a con.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone too little change is to cheat them, so it means swindle.

clue.text: Prohibition sees cop retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for cop is read backwards

parts.note: to cop someone is to catch or nab them

explanation.surface: A ban comes in as a police officer retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop' looks like a police officer but is the verb meaning catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A prohibition is an official order forbidding something, a synonym.

clue.text: Understanding blame attached to harbour

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Mutual understanding is reached when blame is pinned on a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, sympathetic relationship in which people understand each other.

clue.text: Alpine sun transformed narrow piece of land

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters of Alpine sun are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mountain sunshine changes a thin strip of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula is land jutting into water, often a narrow projection almost surrounded by sea.

clue.text: A lot of criticism about a source of television interference

indicators.note: the shortened word goes about the other letters
a lot of, not all of, the word for criticism, so its last letter goes

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism

indicators.note: the source of television is its first letter

explanation.surface: Plenty of complaints about something that ruins TV reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims STICK to STIC, which goes 'about' A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is crackling noise from atmospheric electricity that disrupts radio and TV signals.

clue.text: Peak support involving husband and lots of characters

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the husband's letter goes inside

parts.note: an alp is a mountain peak
to abet is to support or assist

explanation.surface: A mountain prop involving a husband and a large cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people in a story; here it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of letters used to write a language contains many written symbols.

clue.text: Kidnapping ending in distress, of course

indicators.note: the ending of the word distress is its last letter

parts.note: natch is slang short for naturally, meaning of course

explanation.surface: A kidnapping ends in distress, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is slang for an abduction or a grab, as in a child snatch.

clue.text: Bananas: food without energy? That's a nuisance

parts.note: a hand is a bunch of bananas

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the energy letter is removed

parts.note: food is fuel for the body
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Crazy: food with no energy in it? What a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like 'crazy', an anagram signal; it is the bunch of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult child or task is called a handful: troublesome, hard to manage.

clue.text: Top setter's hard attitude with posh lass

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an air is a manner or attitude
gel is an upper-class pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: The best crossword compiler has a tough manner and an upper-class girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top setter' looks like the best compiler; it is something that sets the hair on top of your head.
explanation.definitionFit: A product applied to the head that holds a hairstyle in place is a setter for the top.

clue.text: Time to interrupt that chap (an assassin)

indicators.note: the time letter breaks into the word for that chap

parts.note: him refers to that chap

explanation.surface: Time to break in on that man, a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer is an assassin: someone paid to murder.

clue.text: Cordiality on leaving some time after conflict

indicators.note: the shortened month comes after the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: on leaving means the letters o and n are taken out

parts.note: a month is some time

explanation.surface: Friendliness returns some time after a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on leaving' takes ON out of MONTH, leaving MTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth is friendliness and affection, a synonym for cordiality.

clue.text: A positive outcome, losing one's beard

indicators.note: losing tells us to drop a letter from the word for positive outcome

parts.note: a win is a positive outcome
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone wins something but has to shave off their beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard' is the bristly fringe on an ear of barley or other grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call the bristle on a grass head its beard; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Show of embarrassment, seeing how poor people live?

definitions.meaning: covering one's lips with a palm is a gesture of embarrassment
the phrase describes living with just enough for immediate needs

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a literal gesture of putting a palm to the lips, and the idiom for a precarious, subsistence existence.

clue.text: America adopting universal line regarding customs?

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the universal letter goes inside

parts.note: USA is America
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: America takes on a universal stance on customs duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customs' looks like border controls but means habits.
explanation.definitionFit: The habitual or normal is what follows custom, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Regret monarch's being besieged by heads of Merchant Navy

indicators.note: the monarch's word is surrounded by the two first letters
the heads of Merchant and Navy are their first letters

parts.note: a monarch uses the royal 'our' for 'my'

explanation.surface: A king laments that the merchant fleet has him under siege.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn is to grieve or feel sorrow for a loss, a sense close to regret.

clue.text: Ostentatious sob recalled as something generating red eyes?

parts.note: flash is informal for showy or ostentatious

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for sob runs backwards

parts.note: to blub is to sob

explanation.surface: A showy person's crying, remembered as the cause of their red eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Red eyes suggest weeping, fitting the sob; in fact they are the red-eye effect in photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: An old camera's one-use bright lamp could reflect off retinas, giving people red eyes in photos.

clue.text: Hot team in card game making cut

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
East and West form a partnership in bridge

explanation.surface: A winning partnership in a card game is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players sit as North, South, East and West, playing in two pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop or cut, as with an axe.

clue.text: Hotel regularly accommodating a divine

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the word for regularly takes in the letter a

parts.note: evenly means regularly, at a steady rate

explanation.surface: A hotel that routinely puts up a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like a noun, a churchman, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine and heavenly both mean of or like God or paradise, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Fairly dim idiot concealing bad cut

indicators.note: the word for idiot hides the shortened word inside it

parts.note: a twit is an idiot

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word for bad loses its last letter

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A not-very-bright idiot hiding a nasty wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly dim' looks like a description of the idiot but is the definition. 'cut' shortens ILL to IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit means lit by twilight, so only dimly lit rather than fully dark.
